original_finding.title: Every managed request and heartbeat is serialized behind one global queue and synchronous state-file fsync

root_cause.summary: mutateState combines two distinct responsibilities: single-process serialization and durable checkpointing. Every call unconditionally invokes writeFileAtomicSync, even for runtime-only in-flight counters and activity timestamps that are explicitly reset after a process restart.
evidence: src/stcontrol.js:340-348 serializes every mutation on one process-wide queue and always calls persistState.
src/stcontrol.js:277-280 performs mkdirSync plus writeFileAtomicSync of the complete JSON state.
src/stcontrol.js:980-1000 persists request admission; src/stcontrol.js:1005-1011 persists request completion, producing two full-file writes per request.
src/stcontrol.js:294-303 resets all in-flight counters on restart, proving these counters are runtime state rather than recovery evidence.

durability_required_callers: mode, lease, gate and nonce changes
dependency_map.shared_resource: stateQueue and one adapter-state.json file across all users

remediation_plan.strategy: Retain one short serialized admission critical section for correctness, but separate serialization from persistence and persist only durable state transitions.

steps.change: Introduce a queue helper whose mutator can explicitly request durable persistence; keep the existing durable wrapper as the default so control-plane callers remain fail-safe.
Perform lease, gate, durable-session validation and in-flight increment atomically in that queue. Managed reads/writes update runtime counters without a synchronous file write.
For an independent write, create the pending-sync marker in the same admission section and force persistence before next(); do not weaken the recovery evidence boundary.

Make finish/close counter decrements volatile. Coalesce lastSeen/lastPage activity into a bounded checkpoint rather than fsyncing every heartbeat; session creation/logout and mode/gate/lease transitions stay immediate.

Add instrumentation-friendly tests that stub write-file-atomic and assert a managed request/finish and page heartbeat do not cause per-event durable writes, while independent write admission does persist its marker before next().

remediation_plan.rollback: The durable wrapper remains the default. A rollback can route all mutations through it again without changing the state schema.

benefits: Removes two synchronous full-state writes from each ordinary request.
Prevents unrelated users from waiting on disk I/O while preserving serialized authorization.
Keeps pending independent writes, gates, leases and operation idempotency crash durable.
risks: Activity timestamps may lag by the checkpoint interval after a crash.
A careless volatile classification could lose a recovery-critical pending-sync marker.
mitigations: Explicitly default mutations to durable and opt only enumerated runtime callers into volatile mode.
Test that independent admission persists before invoking next().
Keep the existing restart-time in-flight reset behavior.

reassessed_severity.justification: The finding is directly reachable on every tracked request and scales across all users, but it is a performance/availability bottleneck rather than an authorization bypass by itself.
